s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of Zero Hour in the Indian Parliament?
o: It is a device borrowed from the British Parliament
It is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure of both Houses
It is an informal parliamentary innovation and is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure
It is expressly mentioned in the Constitution
x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian innovation. It is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure and has been in use since 1962; it was not borrowed from another country.
tq: Distinguish a formal constitutional or rule-based device from an informal parliamentary practice.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s: With reference to Zero Hour in the Rajya Sabha, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It follows Question Hour and has a fixed duration of one hour
It is held only after the day's regular agenda is completed
It is not permitted in the Rajya Sabha
It precedes Question Hour, during which urgent public matters may be raised
x: In the Rajya Sabha, urgent matters of public importance are raised during the first hour, before Question Hour.
tq: Separate the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha arrangements instead of applying the Lok Sabha sequence to both Houses.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Zero Hour:
1. It has no fixed duration prescribed in the Rules.
2. It continues until the regular business of the day is taken up in the Lok Sabha.
3. A member must give the same prior notice as is required for an ordinary question.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Zero Hour has no fixed duration in the Rules and in the Lok Sabha lasts until the day's regular agenda is taken up. Members do not give the prior notice required for an ordinary question; they intimate the Presiding Officer on the same day.
tq: Test the distinction between same-day intimation for Zero Hour and formal prior notice for questions.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s: Who decides which members may raise matters during Zero Hour?
x: Members intimate the Presiding Officer on the same day, and the Presiding Officer decides whom to allow to raise a matter.
tq: Use the question 'who would do this job?' to identify the authority controlling parliamentary proceedings.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of matters raised during Zero Hour?
o: The Presiding Officer decides which members may be allowed to raise them
Members may raise them without the prior notice required for a question
Ministers are constitutionally bound to give an immediate reply
They concern urgent matters of public importance
x: Ministers are not bound to reply to matters raised during Zero Hour. The other features correctly describe the procedure.
tq: Find the single statement that reverses a procedural limitation.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s: When the Chair issues a direction or an assurance is given in relation to a matter raised during Zero Hour, which institution sends the extract to the concerned Ministry for action?
x: The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs sends the relevant extract to the concerned Ministry when the Chair issues a direction or an assurance is given.
tq: Identify the administrative body associated with follow-up action on parliamentary assurances and directions.
sec: Zero Hour - timing, notice, duration, origin, Rules status  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to a no-confidence motion, consider the following statements:
1. It is expressly mentioned in the Constitution.
2. Its constitutional basis is connected with Article 75(3).
3. It may be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
4. It requires the support of 50 members for leave to be granted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: A no-confidence motion is not expressly mentioned in the Constitution. It flows from Article 75(3), is moved only in the Lok Sabha, and requires the support of 50 members for leave.
tq: Trap the incorrect constitutional-status statement while checking House, support and Article details separately.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: A no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha is moved under which Rule of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business?
x: A no-confidence motion is moved under Rule 198 of the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.
tq: Test precise rule-number recall using nearby numerical distractors.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements about a no-confidence motion is correct?
o: Reasons for moving it must necessarily be stated
It can be moved in either House of Parliament
It can be moved only by the Leader of the Opposition
x: The Speaker exercises discretion in admitting or rejecting a no-confidence motion. Reasons need not be stated, and the motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' test to distinguish the Speaker's procedural role from political roles.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: If a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, what is the constitutional consequence?
o: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved
The concerned Minister must resign, while the Council continues
Only the Prime Minister must resign
The entire Council of Ministers must resign
x: The motion tests the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha. If passed, the whole Council of Ministers must resign.
tq: Connect the procedural outcome with the constitutional principle of collective responsibility.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: The first no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers was moved against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963 by:
x: The first no-confidence motion against Jawaharlal Nehru was moved in 1963 by J.B. Kripalani.
tq: Link the event, year and mover rather than relying on the event alone.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly describes the no-confidence motion moved against the Andhra State ministry in November 1954?
o: It was moved by Gouthu Latchanna and carried by 69 votes to 68
It was moved by Gouthu Latchanna and defeated by 68 votes to 69
It was moved by J.B. Kripalani and defeated by 69 votes to 68
It resulted in the continuation of the Prakasam ministry for five years
x: Gouthu Latchanna's motion in November 1954 was carried by 69 votes to 68. The Prakasam ministry consequently fell after 13 months.
tq: Use the vote margin and mover together to avoid swapping a closely related historical instance.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Andhra State ministry in chronological order:
A. Prakasam ministry fell by one vote
B. President's Rule ended
C. No-confidence motion moved by Gouthu Latchanna
D. President's Rule was imposed
x: The motion was moved in November 1954, the Prakasam ministry fell by one vote, President's Rule was imposed on 16 November 1954, and it ended on 27 March 1955.
tq: Fix the sequence using the dated beginning and end of President's Rule and then place the immediate political events.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: The no-confidence motion is regarded as the most powerful weapon of executive accountability because it:
o: permits the Speaker to dismiss individual Ministers
enables the Rajya Sabha to remove the Council of Ministers
enforces the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha
x: A no-confidence motion directly enforces the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.
tq: Choose the option that states the constitutional effect rather than a procedural side-effect.
sec: No-confidence motion - constitutional status, support, reasons, Speaker's role, instances  [APPSC]

s: Question Hour in the Lok Sabha is generally held during:
o: The first hour of every sitting
Only the first sitting of each week
The hour immediately before the day's adjournment
The last hour of every sitting
x: Question Hour is held during the first hour of every sitting of the Lok Sabha, when Ministers answer questions.
tq: Test the standard time slot without confusing it with the different Rajya Sabha Zero Hour sequence.
sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following correctly matches the type of question with its answer and supplementary-question position?
1. Starred question — Oral answer — Supplementaries allowed
2. Unstarred question — Written answer — Supplementaries not allowed
3. Short-notice question — Oral answer — Supplementaries allowed
4. Question to a private member — Oral or written answer
Which of the above are correctly matched?
x: All four matches are correct. Starred and short-notice questions receive oral answers with supplementaries allowed; unstarred questions receive written answers without supplementaries; a question to a private member may receive an oral or written answer.
tq: Check each row independently, especially the answer mode and supplementary-question rule.
sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Question to a private member — Blue paper
x: A question addressed to a private member is printed on yellow paper, not blue paper. Starred, unstarred and short-notice questions are associated with green, white and light pink paper respectively.
tq: Use the comparison table to locate the single altered colour designation.
sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

s: A short-notice question differs from an ordinary question in that it may be admitted when notice is given:
o: Only on the day of the sitting
At least 15 clear days in advance
x: A short-notice question is one for which notice is given less than 10 days in advance. Ordinary questions require at least 15 clear days' notice.
tq: Discriminate between the two notice thresholds instead of treating all questions alike.
sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is considered the most effective method of day-to-day vigilance over the executive?
x: Question Hour is regarded as the most effective method of day-to-day vigilance over the executive because Ministers are required to answer questions.
tq: Match the parliamentary device with its principal accountability function.
sec: Question Hour - timing, types of questions, answers, notice  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is NOT included among the recognised tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
o: Judicial review by the Supreme Court
x: Judicial review is a constitutional function of the judiciary, not a parliamentary device listed among the tools of legislative control over the executive.
tq: Separate parliamentary control devices from mechanisms belonging to another constitutional organ.
sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following are tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
1. Question Hour
2. Calling Attention motion
3. Committee system
4. Budget approval
5. Motion of Thanks
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Question Hour, Calling Attention motion, the committee system, budget approval and the Motion of Thanks are all tools of parliamentary control over the executive.
tq: Recognise a complete list while checking whether the final item has been omitted from the coded options.
sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly compares the devices used by Parliament and State Legislatures for controlling the executive?
o: State Legislatures cannot use Question Hour or motions
Parliament alone uses these devices; State Legislatures use only debates
State Legislatures use the same devices, along with estimates and public accounts committees
State Legislatures use only the no-confidence motion
x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices for executive control and also use estimates and public accounts committees.
tq: Test the Union–State comparison by identifying the correct extension rather than an exclusive claim.
sec: Tools of parliamentary control over the executive  [APPSC]

s: A member raises an objection that the proceedings of the House are departing from the Rules or the Constitution. Which device is being used?
x: A point of order is raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution. There is no debate on it, and the Presiding Officer gives the ruling.
tq: Identify the device from the procedural situation rather than from its name alone.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A point of order is raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution.
2. A point of order is itself subject to a regular debate in the House.
3. The Presiding Officer rules on a point of order.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. A point of order is not subject to regular debate; the Presiding Officer rules on it.
tq: Use the procedural consequence to reject the statement that adds an impermissible debate.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Simple closure — Only important clauses are debated
Closure by compartments — All pending clauses are voted on when time ends
Kangaroo closure — Only important clauses are debated and the others are taken as passed
Guillotine — Matter is declared sufficiently discussed and put to vote
x: Under Kangaroo closure, only important clauses are debated and the remaining clauses are taken as passed. Simple closure and guillotine have the meanings given to other options.
tq: Discriminate among similar closure terms by matching each device with its exact operation.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s: In parliamentary procedure, 'closure by compartments' means that:
o: A member gives way to the Chair
All pending clauses are put to vote without discussion at the end of allotted time
Clauses are grouped into parts and debated and voted upon part by part
Only the first clause is debated and all others are rejected
x: Under closure by compartments, clauses are grouped into parts, with debate and voting taking place part by part.
tq: Distinguish a structured, part-by-part closure from guillotine and yielding the floor.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s: What is meant by 'guillotine' in parliamentary procedure?
o: Only important clauses are selected for debate
All pending clauses are put to vote when the allotted time ends, even if they have not been discussed
The Presiding Officer terminates the membership of a disorderly member
The House adjourns without taking a vote
x: Guillotine refers to putting all pending clauses to vote when the allotted time expires, including clauses that have not been discussed.
tq: Use the time-limit clue and distinguish automatic voting from selective debate.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s: When a member who is speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair, the procedure is known as:
x: Yielding the floor occurs when the member speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair.
tq: Match the ordinary procedural action with its precise parliamentary term.
sec: Point of order, closure, guillotine, yielding the floor  [APPSC]

s: The office of Whip in the Indian parliamentary system derives its authority primarily from:
o: The Rules of Procedure of Parliament
A specific provision of the Constitution
x: The office of Whip is not mentioned in the Constitution, the Rules of the House or any parliamentary statute. It is based on conventions of parliamentary government.
tq: Distinguish a conventional office from a constitutional, statutory or rule-based office.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding a party Whip:
1. Each political party appoints a Whip or Chief Whip.
2. The Whip seeks to ensure attendance and voting according to the party line.
3. Defiance of a Whip can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. A party Whip enforces party discipline regarding attendance and voting, and defiance in relevant circumstances may attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
tq: Check whether all statements describe connected functions and consequences of party discipline.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Whip:

List-I (Type)
A. One-line Whip
B. Two-line Whip
C. Three-line Whip

List-II (Purpose)
1. Strict voting direction
2. Informative communication
3. Direction to attend the House

Select the correct code:
x: A one-line Whip is informative, a two-line Whip directs members to attend, and a three-line Whip gives a strict voting direction.
tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with swapped functions.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s: Which Union Minister maintains close contact with the Chief Whips of political parties in both Houses of Parliament?
o: Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
x: The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs keeps close contact with the Chief Whips of parties in both Houses.
tq: Use the functional association between parliamentary coordination and the concerned ministry.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to parliamentary committees, consider the following statements:
1. The Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha was constituted on 4 March 1997.
2. The Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was constituted on 16 May 2000.
3. The Committee on Empowerment of Women in both Houses was constituted on 29 April 1997.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three dates are correct: 4 March 1997 for the Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee, 16 May 2000 for the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee and 29 April 1997 for the Committee on Empowerment of Women.
tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates before selecting the combined option.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the Committee of Privileges?
o: Lok Sabha—10 members nominated by the Chairman; Rajya Sabha—15 members nominated by the Speaker
Lok Sabha—15 members nominated by the Speaker; Rajya Sabha—10 members nominated by the Chairman
Both Houses—15 members elected by the respective Houses
Both Houses—10 members nominated by the President
x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker, while the Rajya Sabha Committee has 10 members nominated by the Chairman.
tq: Check both membership and nominating authority; the two Houses are deliberately reversed in distractors.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s:
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio Chairperson of which of the following committees?
1. Business Advisory Committee
2. Rules Committee
3. General Purposes Committee

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Speaker is ex-officio Chairperson of the Business Advisory Committee, the Rules Committee and the General Purposes Committee.
tq: Identify the common constitutional-office relationship across the listed committees.
sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

s: An Adjournment Motion in Parliament can be admitted only when it concerns:
o: A demand for grant requiring reduction by one rupee
Any matter raised without prior notice
A matter of definite and urgent public importance
x: An Adjournment Motion sets aside the normal business of the House to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance.
tq: Match the motion with its defining procedural condition rather than with a related device.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about an Adjournment Motion:
1. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. It requires the support of 50 members.
3. It has an element of censure.
4. Its debate lasts at least two hours and thirty minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct. An Adjournment Motion is a Lok Sabha device, requires 50 members' support, carries an element of censure and involves debate of at least two hours and thirty minutes.
tq: Test the House, numerical requirement, character and duration together.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following motions is available in both Houses and seeks an authoritative statement from a Minister?
x: A Calling Attention Motion is available in both Houses and seeks an authoritative statement from the concerned Minister.
tq: Use the combination of House availability and procedural purpose to identify the motion.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: The Calling Attention procedure is significant because it is:
o: An Indian innovation introduced in 1962 but not included in the Rules
An Indian innovation introduced in 1954 and included in the Rules of Procedure
x: Calling Attention is an Indian innovation dating from 1954 and is provided for in the Rules of Procedure.
tq: Discriminate between the dates and rule status of Calling Attention and Zero Hour.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Privilege Motion — Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha
2. Privilege Motion — Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha
3. Cut Motion — Demands for Grants
4. Calling Attention — Both Houses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairs are correct. Privilege matters are governed by Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha; cut motions relate to demands for grants, while Calling Attention is available in both Houses.
tq: Verify each motion against both its procedural rule and its House or subject scope.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: A motion concerning a breach of privilege by a Minister or a Member is governed by which of the following rules?
o: Rule 198 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 377 in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 377 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 180A in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 184 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 193 in the Rajya Sabha
x: Privilege matters are governed by Rule 222 of the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 of the Rajya Sabha.
tq: Avoid rule-number swaps by associating the lower and upper Houses separately.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a Censure Motion from a No-confidence Motion?
o: A No-confidence Motion may be moved in either House
Censure requires reasons to be stated, whereas No-confidence does not require reasons
Passing a Censure Motion necessarily forces the Council of Ministers to resign
Censure is directed only against the entire Council of Ministers, whereas No-confidence may target one Minister
x: A Censure Motion must state reasons, while a No-confidence Motion need not state reasons. Censure may target a Minister, a group or the whole Council, whereas No-confidence is against the entire Council in the Lok Sabha.
tq: Compare the requirement, target and consequence instead of relying on the names alone.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Censure Motion may be directed against a Minister, a group of Ministers or the whole Council of Ministers.
2. A No-confidence Motion is directed against the entire Council of Ministers.
3. Passing a Censure Motion compels the Council of Ministers to resign.
4. Passing a No-confidence Motion requires the Council of Ministers to resign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because passing a Censure Motion does not compel resignation, whereas passing a No-confidence Motion does.
tq: Find the single reversed consequence in a comparison table.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: A No-confidence Motion in the Lok Sabha is governed by which rule and requires the support of how many members for admission?
x: A No-confidence Motion is governed by Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha and requires the support of 50 members.
tq: Pair the correct rule number with the specific numerical threshold.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: Who decides whether a No-confidence Motion is in order and admits or rejects it?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a No-confidence Motion is in order and admits or rejects it.
tq: Ask which presiding authority performs the procedural gatekeeping function.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the type of Cut Motion?
o: Policy Cut — reduction of the demand to Re 1
Economy Cut — reduction of the demand to Rs 100
Token Cut — reduction by an amount representing total rejection of policy
Policy Cut — reduction by a specified amount without expressing policy disapproval
x: A Policy Cut proposes reduction of the demand to Re 1 to express disapproval of the policy. An Economy Cut involves a specified reduction, while a Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 to ventilate a specific grievance.
tq: Distinguish the three cut motions by the amount and purpose of reduction.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Cut Motions:
1. They are moved on demands for grants.
2. An Economy Cut proposes reduction by a specified amount.
3. A Token Cut proposes reduction by Rs 100 to indicate a specific grievance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Cut Motions relate to demands for grants and include policy, economy and token cuts with their respective forms of reduction.
tq: Use the common subject first, then verify the distinctive numerical feature of Token Cut.
sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding parliamentary questions is correct?
o: An Unstarred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions
A Starred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions
A Starred Question receives a written answer and permits no supplementary question
Both Starred and Unstarred Questions necessarily receive oral answers
x: A Starred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions. An Unstarred Question receives a written answer and does not permit supplementary questions.
tq: Separate the paired devices through the answer mode and availability of supplementaries.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: A Short Notice Question is intended for a matter of urgent public importance and may be asked with:
x: A Short Notice Question concerns an urgent matter of public importance and is asked with less than 10 days' notice. It receives an oral answer.
tq: Identify the exceptional notice period attached to an urgent procedural device.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following statements about Question Hour is correct?
o: It is an unscheduled period during which Ministers are not required to respond
It is the last hour of every sitting and is devoted only to private members' business
It is the first hour of every sitting during which Ministers answer questions
It is available only when an Adjournment Motion is admitted
x: Question Hour is the first hour of every sitting. Ministers answer questions during this period, which enables members to seek information and exercise control over the executive.
tq: Distinguish a formally scheduled device from the unscheduled Zero Hour.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Zero Hour?
o: It precedes Question Hour and is confined to starred questions
It is a device available only in the Rajya Sabha
It is expressly provided in the Rules of Procedure and requires ministers to reply to every matter
It is the time after Question Hour, permits matters to be raised without prior notice, and is not provided in the Rules of Procedure
x: Zero Hour follows Question Hour, allows members to raise important matters without prior notice, does not bind Ministers to reply and is not included in the Rules of Procedure. It is an Indian innovation associated with 1962.
tq: Separate Zero Hour from Question Hour and Calling Attention by notice, rule status and ministerial response.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: The parliamentary device associated with matters that are not points of order and are raised under Rule 377 in the Lok Sabha is:
x: Rule 377 of the Lok Sabha permits members to raise matters that are not points of order. The corresponding device in the Rajya Sabha is known as Special Mentions.
tq: Match the exact rule number with the formal name used in the concerned House.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Rule 377, Lok Sabha — Matters not raisable under any other device
2. Special Mentions, Rajya Sabha — Equivalent device to Rule 377 matters
3. Rule 193, Lok Sabha — Short-duration discussion without voting
4. Rule 184, Lok Sabha — Discussion followed by voting

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: All four pairs are correct. Rule 377 and Special Mentions serve corresponding purposes in the two Houses, while Rules 193 and 184 distinguish discussions without and with voting respectively.
tq: Start with rule-number pairs and then confirm the presence or absence of voting.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: A discussion under Rule 193 of the Lok Sabha is characterised by:
o: A reduction of a demand for grant to Re 1
No voting and a short-duration format
A compulsory vote at its conclusion
A requirement that the matter be a breach of privilege
x: Rule 193 provides for a short-duration discussion without voting. Rule 184, in contrast, provides for discussion followed by a vote.
tq: Use the voting consequence to distinguish Rules 193 and 184.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s:
Arrange the following parliamentary discussion devices in chronological order of their introduction or institutional association:
A. Calling Attention
B. Short-duration discussion
C. Zero Hour

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Short-duration discussion is an Indian innovation of 1953, Calling Attention dates from 1954, and Zero Hour is associated with 1962. Therefore, the correct order is B, A, C.
tq: Place the dated devices first and compare the closely spaced years 1953, 1954 and 1962.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s:
A Short-duration Discussion in the Lok Sabha has which of the following features?
1. It is limited to a maximum of two hours.
2. It is an Indian innovation of 1953.
3. It necessarily ends with a formal vote.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because a short-duration discussion does not involve voting.
tq: Identify the duration and origin while rejecting the false voting consequence.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: A half-an-hour discussion is intended for:
o: A matter that can be raised only through a No-confidence Motion
A demand for grant requiring reduction by Rs 100
A matter already sufficiently debated but requiring factual elucidation
A breach of privilege requiring immediate suspension of the House
x: A half-an-hour discussion is held on a matter that has been sufficiently debated but requires further factual elucidation. It involves no formal motion or vote.
tq: Apply the purpose of the device to a scenario requiring clarification rather than a fresh decision.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Half-an-hour discussion — formal motion followed by voting
x: The fourth pair is incorrect. A half-an-hour discussion does not involve a formal motion or voting; it is meant for factual elucidation on a matter already debated.
tq: Find the procedural feature that contradicts the defining nature of the device.
sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

s:
With reference to resolutions in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A resolution is a self-contained proposal.
2. Every resolution is a substantive motion.
3. A mover may withdraw a resolution at any time without the leave of the House.
4. A resolution must be put to vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
